text:
camille: Quick flag — DSAR pipeline reported a partial delete for ephemeral embeddings. Not all vectors marked as deleted, and KMS shows intermittent decrypt errors. Anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: saw one alert earlier. looks like a 403 from KMS for the ephemeral keystore service account.

olivia: which SA? the dsar-backfill runner or the keystore-proxy?

raj: dsar-backfill@redwood-prod. Error snippet: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-20T14:02:17Z keystore: decrypt failed key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/priv/cryptoKeys/ephemeral-1 err=permission denied
```

camille: thanks. That would explain partial deletes — if decrypt fails we bail and leave tombstone incomplete. Might be related to last night's IAM cleanup.

security-bot: :rotating_light: IAM change detected 2026-03-20T02:11:09Z by svc:infra-automation@github-actions with message "remove unused roles". Affected binding: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on serviceAccount:dsar-backfill@redwood-prod.

maria: legal; if deletes are incomplete we need to log scope and impact. Can you collect the list of subject IDs affected? We may need to notify the requester if full erasure didn't propagate.

ops-joe: I'll run a query against the erasure ledger to find rows with status != deleted AND last_attempt >= 2026-03-20T02:00Z.

camille: good. also need to confirm audit logs for who accessed the key during that window and whether any decrypts succeeded (so we can prove no accidental exposure).

raj: quick workaround: re-add the decrypter role to dsar-backfill SA and requeue backfill with --resume-mode=decrypt-only. That should resume KV decrypt to mark tombstones.

olivia: before we do that, can we confirm the service account wasn't intentionally privileged? security wants a short blast radius (least privilege). Maybe use keystore-proxy token exchange flow instead of giving direct KMS role.

camille: agree. short-term: restore role, run backfill, then replace with proxy path and revoke role. Long-term: baked fix in erasure service to retry transient decrypts with exponential backoff and fallback to queued tombstone retry to avoid leaving partial states.

ops-joe: running query now. returning ~112 subject_ids. I'll dump to secure Drive and share to #eng-security-private.

security-bot: audit snippet: 
```
protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="svc:infra-automation@github-actions"
resourceName="projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/priv/cryptoKeys/ephemeral-1"
```

maria: ok — good to know who did the change. Legal wants a timeline and proof-of-retry. We should capture: list of affected requests, repro steps, and final status after re-run.

camille: I'll open an internal incident doc and link the DSAR IDs. Plan: 1) restore role (ops-joe), 2) requeue decrypt-only backfill (raj), 3) collect proofs & logs (camille + olivia), 4) replace SA access with proxy token workflow and test (olivia + raj), 5) revoke role and close (security).

raj: one more note — there's a subtle edge: some records are stored encrypted at rest with per-tenant key rotation. If decrypt fails for rotated keys we need key version mapping. I'll include that in the backfill run to avoid false negatives.

ops-joe: role restored at 5376543290. starting backfill. job id backfill-ephem-5376.

erasure-bot: backfill-ephem-5376 status: started (workers=8). progress: 0/112. ETA: ~18m.

camille: awesome. raj/olivia — can you prepare a short postmortem blurb so legal can send the requester if needed? keep it factual: cause, remediation, and verification steps.

olivia: will do. also adding a follow-up ticket to add a guard: fail-open must not leave partial deletes — instead retry and flag for ops after N attempts.

maria: thanks team. once finished, please cc me and include audit pointers for proving no plaintext leak.

camille: loop closing: will update when backfill completes and attach logs. thanks all :heart:
